verdict.tagline: Endless galactic strategy hampered by mounting technical hurdles and steep learning.
for_you_if: you enjoy deep and complex grand strategy systems
you have patience for steep learning curves

you want to avoid separate third-party launchers
you are sensitive to expensive expansion pack costs

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game has a steep learning curve and requires watching external guides or tutorials to understand.

citations.review_text:
OK this is a really cool game. 
I'm six hours into the game, which means I've dedicated 9 hours to the game:
-10 mins looking into the store page and looking through reviews; turns out there's a steep learning curve and expensive DLC catalogue
-30 mins figuring out if the game is worth full price, whether DLC is worth getting
-20 mins finding whether the game is on sale anywhere, how often sales are, deciding whether I can be bothered waiting for one
-2 hours watching youtube videos of how to play and trying to remember as much as possible
and finally:
-6 hours of playing the actual game.

It turns out the game is very fun so full price isn't such a bad deal, despite it being weird to keep the game at this price when it's so old.

Good sandbox elements, good RP elements, good 4X gameplay and surprisingly good exploration for a 4X game where usually you don't discover much of anything whereas in this game exploration feels rewarding. Coming from other 4X games, diplomacy is genuinely deep compared to most games and allows you to fuck with or not fuck with anyone you want in any way you want which is nice.

A tutorial is definitely necessary to avoid headaches unless you're hardcore but once you get the basics the underlying game is very fun. Recommend for who you'd expect - geeks, sci-fi, 4X, and grand strategy fans, etc. - but also for those who like games with deep procedural storytelling like RimWorld; I haven't gotten far enough to know how repetitive it gets but so far the stories generated have been interesting, impactful and non-immersion-breaking, which I like because I like nice and enjoyable things in life in general ok bye

Do yourself a favor, invest some time like an hour or two into watching a guide and familarising yourself with all the menus. You will be addicted. This game is like crack, you will completely lose track fo time.
watch as many guides as possible you will need it

claims.claim: Reviewers report optimization problems and bugs introduced alongside updates.

citations.review_text: Optimization problems that come with updates, tasks that become monotonous as the game progresses. I do not recommend.

Paradox greed has brought the game into a completely broken state. New DLCs motivated by insatiable greed are released faster than the newly introduced bugs can be fixed. The technical debt is larger and larger with every DLC released - it's like a cancer killing formerly solid games via uncontrollable growth. And it's not just Stellaris, HOI4 is the same case - only old games like Crusader Kings 2 that are no longer updated are safe. If you read "Paradox Interactive", run!

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the pricing model for downloadable content as expensive and excessive.

citations.review_text: Its good but very greedy DLC arnt worth there price played thousands of hours on playstation and own all the DLC's on there but hard to talk my pc friend to invest in an old game that cost 400 bucks

Really liked this game for the early sections of it. The scheming and strategizing is really fun. You have so many options for how you run your faction as well as the faction customization itself.

I would only recommend this game if your are into something complex like magic or maybe like hardcore DND. The late game has so many things to keep track of its overwhelming in a bad way. Its fun to have so many options but it just becomes a slog around the 2-6 hour mark for me. 

I've even gone to the workshop for some mods to stream line some of the menus but its just a mountain of screens and pop ups pretty much constantly.

Outside the gameplay itself the DLC is dumb. Its (imo) some minor cosmetic or function changes to the factions creator that are not worth the money. In the end you'll likely only really develop one way of playing the game since you need a Stellaris PHD to try and run the game from various different strategies. So the extra fodder content is just a money grab and man are the prices crazy. The Nomad DLC alone is atm 25$ which is wild to price a DLC that does so little that high.

TLDR; 
Good game 6/10
DLC is greedy AF
Graphics are Meh serviceable
Can kinda do whatever you want if your willing to learn.
Gameplay is overly complicated in good and bad ways.
Lotta content if you can get into the game and learn it but its a mountain of stuff to track.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game suffers from poor optimization and performance issues in the endgame.

citations.review_text: Poor optimisation at endgame. Bad game mechanics that change all the balance and ruins the game

A game thats 35 USD should give you the full experience. This game, when you buy it for 35 USD, gives you nothing but the bare bones game with no deep features. You have to spend around 200 USD to have a game with proper content. The game lacks character interactions, its combat depth is only ship design, nothing more. The game massively punishes most "fun" and "original" builds and constantly has unbalanced "meta" builds. The rest of the game seems to be balanced around these "meta" builds as well since those fun and original builds are basically impossible to get powerful with without other meta/cheese things. The game is badly optimized and if you decide to play modded which is the only way to actually get good content thats not too shallow, your game will be very laggy and you will spend double the time you spend playing on configuring your mod load order. Thats right, paradox interactive's games, even though they are extremely depending on their mods, do not yet have an automatic load order sorter or even any work done to make the impact of a bad load order even slightly less. They do nothing for modders. Even the slightest update breaks most mods which isnt the case in a lot of other games that depend heavily on modding. They are lazy and do not care about their modders and playerbase. They expect you to buy the game's full experience for 200 dollars then also buy a 3000 dollar pc apparently because thats the only way you are running the game in its max settings but thats still not certain, it will still lag.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features a steep learning curve and requires significant time to understand its complex systems.

citations.review_text:
Finally, a Paradox game that clicks with me. I was going to enslave everyone but
A.) They're just trying to survive 
B.) Some are puppy-dog cute
C.) They have like 20 times the fleet power as me 

The diplomacy system is surprisingly thorough. The menus are intuitive and for as deep as the game is, you will have enough of a rough grasp on the systems within 3-5 hours i'd say. It's really fun finding ways to multiply your productions. I zoned out for a couple hours and quadrupled my alloy production so i could build a screw-you sized fleet. 

The very first hour is a menace, the tutorials are front loaded so i'd suggest just jumping in and starting a save, pick up what you can from the tutorials and mess around. Learn from it and keep trying. You'll lose fleets, science ships, you'll build the "wrong" things, research tech inefficiently - who cares, you're learning and the music is amazing so relax and enjoy! 

This game is also pretty scary to me - not something i was expecting. The cosmic horror here is very, very good and unique in its sense of scale, with awesome writing to convey the genuinely terrifying presence you may have to face.
It's clear that a lot of thought went into this game, enough that the learning curve is a little steep- but if you're willing to learn it's definitely a rewarding experience

Only buy DLC on mega sales like mid and end of year sales where its like 80% off but past that the game is stupidly fun. its the kingpin of empire management. 
modding has tons of support. 
The game is complex and has a steep learning curve but the reward for learning is vast. 

My experience with most dlc and some mods:
I'm playing whats called a frame world where i dont have a planet i have a space station that orbits a black hole. you grow it infinitely instead of finding more planets. it gets pretty nuts and you can even integrate megastructures into your frameworld making it truly awe inspiring. a fortress of solitude. 

for vanilla base players, i still think its great fun. it leaves games like civ in the dust. 
Yes they use ai in their development process but not to literally make the game from the ground up. its touch up work.

Newbie with some 4x game experience early impression.  Full disclosure.  I bought the base plus a few DCs 4 years ago and it cooked me. I think the main reason is I didn't have the time then to give it what it required.  But a couple weeks ago I got reinspired, added a couple new DCs, and now I'm fully engaged. 
 My only experience comparison is with Civ 6 which I have completed a couple campaigns 100+ hrs.  First, the game does little hand holding, there is a steep learning curve out of the box.  Its comprehensive depth is inspiring, but that comes with lots of where do I begin and how do I do and what should I do/prioritize/select moments.  It definitely required I watch some beginner videos for the layout, mechanics, and early game play.  I am thoroughly enjoying the learning of the game but it is not a play for an hour and then a week later jump back in kind of game.  Starting out you should expect to play 2+ hours each session and 3-4 times a week to save you from being frustrated and lost every time you fire it up.  That time is in game not the time you will spend watching learning videos.  I will say AI has been an awesome help and time save in learning.  I often will screen shot research tech options and throw them in AI to give advice. It prioritizes them and gives explanations for its choices. 
This really is a full immersion game where you get lost in the stars (for good reason) for hours on end.  If you can handle that, you won't be disappointed.

Great gameplay mechanics, the controls might be overwhelming at first but the game has a tutorial and easier difficulties for you to get used to the game. This game doesn't feel repetitive at any point as there's always more features and mechanics to focus on- one of the perks of a complex game. The base game has tons of features and it isn't a requirement for DLCs. Overall, this game is very beginner friendly whilst still being very fun for more experienced players.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game incorporates generative AI elements in its development.

citations.review_text: Once upon a time I would have recommended Stellaris, but the use of generative AI makes it a hard no.

Paradox as started using generative AI for development in previously released titles, such as Stellaris. If Paradox's relentless monetisation wasn't enough, like the semi-recent addition of a subscription model for DLC, now its very creation is an ethical concern.

[TL;DR]
1. Buy on sale.
2. Save your wallet, Paradox has stupidly hostile pricing model when it comes to their DLCs, the price does not match the content you get, as a cherry on top moved to using generative AI.
3. Support and care for a different game that's more worth your cash, heart and time.
3a. Buy Rimworld and their DLCs instead, I'd also recommend Starsector, totally not shilling.
4. Workshop is infested with AI mods, though that's the case for most games nowadays.
5. You'll get hundreds or thousands of hours out of the base game alone, 8/10 but I'll have to deduct -2 points regarding Paradox Interactive's recent choices, 6/10.

[Review]
So first things first, buy it on sale, and a warning that it's probably not the same game anymore if you've seen gameplay of it years ago and want to try it now, I learnt that the hard way. I don't doubt that it will continue to change like a non-committal person who can't settle on a status quo, so no matter how much hours you have, updated gameplay guides are your bestfriend.

Don't brother, or at least I wouldn't recommend getting the DLCs, they're stupidly over-priced for so little content for its price and with generative AI content in it. 

If you're thinking of spending more cash on Stellaris, at that point, just get Rimworld and all of its DLCs, I've got over 6,000 hours on it and I'll tell you now it's very much worth it, it also helps that newer DLCs have compatability to previous ones, can't say the same for Stellaris.
Hell, 1.7 is on unstable development right now, which runs on their own in-house engine rather than Unity, I've tried it myself and can tell you now as a low-end laptop gamer, the performance is like chewing mint candy and drinking ice cold water. Absolutely refreshing to see an update entirely focused on performance, a much needed face lift.

Can you tell where my loyalties and love lie with how much I'm shilling, on a review and on a different game no less?

I was quite happy with Stellaris before they started using Generative AI. This negative review will stand until it is removed from the game.

If you want the full experience, it'll cost you upward of $300 (or $10/month). I only have the base game; therefore many structures, ships, and concepts are locked behind the 24+ DLC packs (with more coming!). My experience with Stellaris has thus far been:
* search for something in the in-game help (eg, megastructures)
* fail to get any results or get only the most surface-level description
* look for more information online
* read something promising or tangentially related
* can't find it in-game
* eventually discover it's locked behind DLC
* repeat

2) The game with the DLC is really good. But the price of all of the DLC is pretty insane.
3) Make sure multiplayer works in the 2 hour refund window if that's your reason for buying the game. Though it is still highly recommended even as a pure singleplayer game.

The essay version
3) If want this game for multiplayer and you have a network provider who uses a CGNAT (any phone provider pretending to be a real ISP. T-Mobile Home Internet, Verizon, etc) then I would test this game's multiplayer within the 2 hour refund window. For me, the multiplayer just straight up doesn't work whether I host or join a game. I've only ever had this issue with 1 other game. My main system is Linux, but I also tested on Windows with every troubleshooting step under the sun tested on each machine. The only other cause I can think of would be my ISP.
The DLC is also really good. But simultaneously the biggest downside. Over 10 years this game has built up several paid expansions. Which is fine, and they're all great. But even so it just costs too much money. I'm not going to really entertain the subscription model as a recommendable option, even though I did pay 1 month of it just to see what DLC I liked. If you want to buy the game and all its DLC, you're looking at about $300. The game has more than enough content to make that technically worth it IMO, but it goes without saying that that's a disgustingly large investment for 1 video game.
The price of the main game should probably be permanently dropped, along with the older DLC entries. Or, maybe the main game should stay at full price as older expansions are slowly integrated into base game.

One day i was playing the game with a buddy of mine, then suddenly it started running like shit, freezing up everytime i clicked something.  I closed out of it and attempted re-open it.  game will load to 100 percent then crash.  i never make it to the menu, ive done all the troubleshooting i can think of, and even youtubed some.  this is day 6 of attempting to fix it and it still will not open.  i have no idea what the issue is, due to this i gotta give  a negative review. if anyone can help please let me know.

I have played a lot in stellaris in years, but until today 2026 the game becomes unplayable due to an error in the launcher and because of new dlc costs because of a DLC with bad reviews that that do not buy, because the game gave me an error to unplayable and I can not play anymore. claims.claim: Reviewers report frequent multiplayer desync problems that disrupt session stability.

citations.review_text: I would like the game much more if they fixed the f*cking desyncing so I can actually play multiplayer with the boys

Paradox's DLC model of pushing unfinished content that breaks the game has leeched all the fun out of this game.
Multiplayer is impossible due to the Out of Sync problems that the unfinished DLC causes.  At some point Paradox is going to have to learn that alienating their player base with overprice unfinished DLC that breaks core game mechanics is not the way to stay relevant.

This game is really fun and great with friends, though if you do play with friends then get ready for your enjoyment to be cut off by unfixable desync destroying the save usually when things are getting exciting. If it wasn't for desync I'd play this game much more often but sessions are typically limited to when we've forgotten how bad and guaranteed desync can be.

If you're fine with single player then go ahead but if you would prefer with multiplayer you can either accept that desync will cause you issues or hope that Paradox puts some serious effort into minimising or eliminating desync.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the AI struggles to handle updated mechanics and frequently gets stuck or breaks during wars.

citations.review_text: Game has too many game-breaking bugs. The ai will often be stuck and not do anything during wars and often there is a bug where my invading army will say I am successful but my army gets instantly ejected and the enemy still owns the planet. Have not been able to play a full multiplayer game because of it and single player is very unfun as a result. This is not to mention the performance problems that have gotten worse especially in the late game. Until paradox fixes these issues (which will take a while since Paradox is lazy and very often incompotent) , this game is not worth it.

As of the 4.0 update the AI is now so badly broken it is borderline unplayable. They have been trying to fix this issue with update after update but it is painfully obvious that without some serious work it will not be back to a decent state, Months of waiting and all that has really been happening is more dlc to add to the pile, much of which just tacks on more mechanics that the AI cannot handle, so more adjustments need to be made, and nothing really improves.

This makes me really sad to say because for a long time this was one of my favorite games, and easily my favorite strategy game, but until the issue with the AI is addressed I can't really recommend it anymore.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game has a steep learning curve and requires substantial time to learn mechanics.

citations.review_text: Stellaris has a steep learning curve and criminally overpriced DLC. Paradox also often fails to fully integrate new features before moving on to the next ones, however, overall stellaris is paradigmatic of the complex 4X Grand Strategy genre. It balances an extremely deep set of mechanics with RP elements that give the player creative freedom over the kind of story they want to tell. If like that idea of role playing as a galaxy spanning civilization, and you're willing to sink several hundred hours and half as many dollars into a game, then stellaris way well become your life.

Quick Preview if you're a Lazy bum and you don't wanna read allat
Cons:
1. DLCs are sometimes overpriced
2. Some DLCs should be Free because of just how unfun the game is with no DLC.
3. When new DLCs come out, you can't get a demo or the basics to test if you'd like the DLC.
4. Multiplayer is usually extremely unbalanced if restrictions aren't made
5. Takes 100 hours to learn anything.

Pros:
1. Space is cool
2. Singleplayer well balanced.
3. Options to be Challenging when you're bored.
4. Options to be Simple and Easy when you just want to do something.
5. Extremely replayable
6. Very fun to Roleplay
7. Vast Empire Customization (FINALLY WE CAN CHOOSE BORDER COLOURS AND SHIP COLOURS!!!)
8. Great modding community which adds content you think is missing from the game. (Especially if you want different UI)

I love Stellaris.
Pesonally I don't really recommend it, the DLCs are really expensive and in my opinion could just sometimes be free because they're usually a requirement if you want to have any actual fun in this game.
I would prefer if they made like the basics of a DLC free, like for the Nomads DLC they just allowed you to be a Nomad Empire in the Vanilla game, but actually give you the content for the rest of the Nomads in the DLC, just so the DLCs are both worth it and the base game is much more playable.

But overall the game is amazing, I love roleplaying as an Empire. I love creating stories for my Empires, and I love just the Empire Creation epecially when creating multiple empires and force spawning them so the disgusting randomly generated flags get out of my face, and actually allow the AI Empires to have sentience.
It’s super fun, but without the DLCs it’s kind of bland, and the game takes a long time to get into and understand. If you like games that suck in your brain this one’s great
